MARKET.head: Unified Wine & Grape Symposium returns to Sacramento in January 2027
MARKET.summ: The wine industry has had a tough year, both here in the U.S. and around the world. There has been a steady stream of bad news from all corners of the wine world and precious little good news to balance the scales.
takeaways: The Unified Wine & Grape Symposium meets in Sacramento from January 26 to 28, 2027, billed as America's largest wine industry gathering.
Tuesday's opening general session covers tracing a $35 Napa Cabernet and a $12.99 Sauvignon Blanc back through the supply chain.

MARKET.head: Wine still tops Australian alcohol purchases as drinking falls and spending per visit rises
MARKET.summ: New research shows that wine endures as “the most widely purchased category” in Australia at 55%, followed by spirits at 46% and beer at 44%. The new ‘What’s Driving Australia’s Alcohol Shopper: Consumption, Channels, Promotions and Occasions’ report from Vypr and Shop! ANZ found that 41% of Australians are drinking less than a...
takeaways: Vypr and Shop! ANZ report finds wine is the most purchased alcohol category in Australia at 55% of shoppers.
41% of Australians drink less than a year ago or have stopped, while 6% drink more, the report says.
48% of shoppers now typically spend over $40 per liquor-store visit, up from about 23% a year earlier.

MARKET.head: Marnong Estate releases first Reserve Chardonnay alongside new spring range
MARKET.summ: Marnong Estate has unveiled its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay as a part its new collection of cool-climate expressions from the estate's Sunbury vineyards. The 2024 Reserve Chardonnay leads the new range which features the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay and 2025 Estate Chardonnay, offering “distinct interpretations of the...
takeaways: Marnong Estate, a Sunbury winery, has released its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay, the 2024 vintage, as part of a new cool-climate range.
The spring collection also includes the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay, the 2025 Estate Chardonnay and the 2026 Estate Sangiovese Rosé.
The new releases are available nationally through independent merchants, at the cellar door and online via the winery's website.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes to Chinese buyers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: 23 Moldovan wine and spirits producers exhibit at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12, seeking Chinese importers and distributors.
Chinese customs data shows Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldova's wine production is exported, with the EU taking roughly 60% of exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine's small formats gain ground as moderation and single-person households grow
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22% to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39%, from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Australian households occupied by a single person rose to 26%, from 18% in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules restrict vague wine sustainability claims from September 27
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825 (EmpCo) restricts vague environmental claims on consumer products, including wine, and is enforced from September 27.
Banned terms include unsubstantiated words like eco-friendly, green and clean, plus sustainability badges lacking third-party certification.
Fines for widespread violations can reach four percent of annual turnover, with enforcement left to individual EU member states.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of fine wine trade value as Burgundy's share jumps
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded fine wine value, extending its lead, per Liv-ex market data.
Burgundy's share of traded value rose from 15.7% last week to 20.8% this week.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany rose to 11.6% on EU buyer demand.

CULTURE.head: Restaurant director says guests may ask sommeliers to adjust wine temperature
CULTURE.summ: When it comes to wine temperature, there are a handful of rules. Some are quick tips for when you’re in a pinch like the easy-to-remember 20 minute rule, while others are more nuanced serving guidelines that map out the proper temperature for each style down to the exact degree. Though these time-tested recommendations might...
takeaways: Andrew Elder, director of restaurants for D.C.'s Hive Hospitality, says guests may ask for wine to be chilled more or brought to room temperature.
Elder advises asking questions rather than declaring a wine wrong, since ideal serving temperature depends on the wine style and the moment.
Restaurants can chill a too-warm wine in an ice bucket or freezer, or decant a too-cold one to let it warm.

CULTURE.head: VinePair's tasting panel names its top 50 wines of 2026
CULTURE.summ: Check out the best wines from previous years here! As the tastings department prepares to wrap up another busy year of exploring, analyzing, and enjoying wine here at VinePair HQ, we’re taking a moment to reflect on the best bottles that 2026 had to offer. As is true each year, we had a dazzlingly diverse set of wines to...
takeaways: VinePair's tasting panel ranked its 50 best wines of 2026 at its New York headquarters.
Wines were judged on quality, value, regional diversity and U.S. availability, not blind, with prices known.
Trends noted include Nebbiolo from Piedmont, cool-climate Blaufränkisch from Germany and Slovenia, and lesser-known grapes like Mencía.

CULTURE.head: Marlborough viticulturist Anna Kelland wins 2026 Young Horticulturist of the Year title
CULTURE.summ: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland has won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title, having “excelled” in an intensive two-day competition in Auckland from 4-5 November. Kelland was the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year and therefore went through to represent the viticulture sector in this year’s...
takeaways: Anna Kelland, a Marlborough viticulture technician for Constellation Brands, won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title in Auckland, 4-5 November.
She beat four rivals from grower, arborist, amenity and plant producer sectors, and also won three special awards including the Woolworths Innovation Project Award.
Her prizes total more than $25,000, and Phoebe Scherer, a Bay of Plenty kiwifruit grower, took second place.

CULTURE.head: Seventeen sommeliers name the bottles they always order when spotted
CULTURE.summ: Exploration is one of wine’s greatest virtues. A bottle shop or wine menu can take you from the Rheinessen’s steep hills to the peaks of Mendoza to the sea salt-dusted cliffs of the San Luis Obispo Coast. Even within a single region, drinkers can taste a world of grapes, terroirs, and climates.
takeaways: Seventeen sommeliers were asked which wines they always order when they see them on a menu.
Picks include Lady of the Sunshine Pinot Noir, Les Jardins de la Martinière Shi Ro 2018, and Antinori Tignanello.
Several choices are small-production or scarce bottles that rarely appear on lists, which sommeliers say makes them worth ordering.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI updates agrochemical lookup app on Apple and Google stores
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated its free AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple App Store and Google Play.
The app gives rapid access to information in the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the 'Dog book'.
Users must perform an app update to keep receiving updates for the app on their phone.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Gut Oggau: stunningly original, naturally made wines from Austria’s Burgenland
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Eduard Tscheppe and his wife Stephanie Tscheppe-Eselböck farm 20 hectares of vines in Austria’s Burgenland region, and their
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Eduard and Stephanie Tscheppe farm 20 hectares in Austria's Burgenland under biodynamics, Demeter certified, at their Gut Oggau winery.
They began in 2007 by buying an old estate in Oggau, on the west bank of Lake Neusiedl near the Hungarian border.
Each Gut Oggau wine is named after a fictional character from a family tree, with faces designed by Jung von Matt.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics owe obligations only to those paying their bills, so consumers who want better reviewing should fund the reviewers they like.
Atkin says critics' expertise should be a little above their target audience, and that a reviewer tasting 14 aromas may be of no use to readers who cannot taste them.
Atkin criticises the roughly 30-second tasting ritual used by wine reviewers, comparing judging wine that way to reviewing a movie based on its trailer.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/8/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet the Young Winemakers Reshaping Burgundy Right Now
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Meet the young winemakers in the heart of Burgundy who are tending the vines and shaping the future of wine
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: William Whitehead has taken charge of Domaine Michel Rebourgeon in Pommard, which makes about 20,000 bottles a year from 4.25 hectares.
Pierre Arcelain runs Domaine Michel Arcelain, where the white wine ages 12 months in a concrete egg.
Arthur Thibert works alongside his father Pierre in Corgoloin, overseeing a new cuverie and more sustainable farming.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction notices, and cellar consignments that ordinary search may miss.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions and optional images; Orpheus notifies them when a matching wine is found and connects them to the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bourgueil’s Aurélien Revillot
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Through a Burgundian lens, Cabernet Franc becomes a study of place and terroir, parcel by parcel
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Aurélien Revillot is a relative newcomer to the Bourgueil appellation in the Loire Valley, and his domaine is part of Becky Wasserman's portfolio.
Revillot makes an entry-level cuvée blended from several parcels, while focusing on single-vineyard wines from his best parcels on the slopes.
His domaine had three finished cuvées in May 2022, with two cuvées parcellaires set to join the range from the 2020 vintage.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós's family in Penedès made wine from 1497; in 1872 he produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine.
Cava is made mainly in Penedès, with 95% from the Penedès region within the Comtats de Barcelona Cava zone, centred on Sant Sadurní d'Anoia.
Sumarroca Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava 2022, from Finca Sumarroca, is aged 40 months and priced at $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was set to visit Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
The author highlighted value picks including DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo, and Piqueras' El Abuelo blend of Alicante Bouschet, Monastrell and Syrah.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why I Enjoy Wine Competition Judging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Plus a guide to Le Puy wines - my notes from a recent vertical tasting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Columnist is judging at the Asia Wine Trophy in Daejeon, South Korea, the only competition he knows with a dedicated orange and amber wine panel.
A Georgian Khikhvi amber received mid-90s scores from all six judges, earning instant grand gold without discussion.
Le Puy, a right-bank Bordeaux estate near St. Emilion, left the Francs Côtes de Bordeaux appellation in 2017 and now bottles as Vin de France.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks drop back Sunday, marking the start of what she calls Kitchen Season.
Kitchen Season runs through November and December, when people cook more to mark occasions and cook for others.
Maker lists kitchen tools she uses year-round that become more essential during festive cooking.
